problems.title: Spatial moment matching is not a full-feature information bound
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, Eq. (8), PDF p. 6; Appendix A.4, PDF p. 16; author LossIB.forward, lines 36–49.
claim: Equation (8) writes a conditional KL for the representation; Appendix A.4 uses the weaker description IB-inspired regularization.
analysis: The author's LossIB.forward computes \(R=(2BN\ln2)^{-1}\sum(\mu^2+s^2-1-\ln s^2)\) from spatial moments of a feature map, with \(s^2\) including the implementation's variance stabilizer \(\epsilon\). It does not integrate the conditional law of the whole tensor.

Let \(a=(1,1,-1,-1)\), \(b=(1,-1,1,-1)\), and \(z_k=\sqrt{1-\epsilon}[\cos(2\pi k/M)a+\sin(2\pi k/M)b]\). These maps have zero spatial mean and variance \(1-\epsilon\), so the stabilized moment penalty is zero. An injective finite deterministic code of this form has \(I(X;Z)=\log_2M\) for uniform labels, whereas a constant code has the same penalty and zero information.
result: The moment regularizer does not bound full-tensor information without extra assumptions. The paper already permits a heuristic IB-inspired reading, which is not contradicted; no trained feature reachability or rendering failure is established.
